newsitem.title: OMAN: Bahrain, Oman and Kuwait sign deal linking bourses.
newsitem.headline: Bahrain, Oman and Kuwait sign deal linking bourses.

text.p: Bahrain, Oman and Kuwait signed on Wednesday an accord to link their bourses, a Muscat Securities Exchange (MSE) official said.

"This accord, which will allow cross-listing of shares traded on the three stock exchanges, is the first of its kind at the level of Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) states," MSE's executive president Mahmoud al-Jarwani said.
The six-member GCC political and economic alliance also groups the United Arab Emirates, Saudi Arabia and Qatar.
Bahrain stock exchange officials said the accord would take effect in the new year.
Al-Jarwani estimated that the market value of 170 companies traded on the three exchanges was more than $20 billion.
"This (agreement) will encourage Gulf Cooperation Council citizens to invest more in joint projects," he added.
Bahrain and Oman began cross-listing shares in March 1995 in the first such step in the Gulf.
Bahraini, Omani and Kuwaiti bourses are open to GCC investors. Some listed Bahraini and Omani firms are also open to foreign investors.
